question: When does the shift inspection have to be done?

body.text: A competent person must start it before each shift in which the equipment will be used. It does not have to be finished before work starts. It can be completed during that shift.
A competent person must begin a visual inspection prior to each shift the equipment will be used, which must be completed before or during that shift.
The level check has its own timing: before each shift and after each move and setup.

question: What is the full checklist for the shift inspection?

body.text: These are the minimum items. Controls for maladjustment. Control and drive mechanisms for wear and contamination. Pressurized lines. Hydraulic fluid level. Hooks and latches. Reeving. Some equipment types have added items in other sections, and some rail items have a railroad exception.

question: What happens if the shift inspection finds a deficiency?

body.text: For checklist items (i) through (xiii), and added equipment-specific items, the competent person must immediately decide whether it is a safety hazard. If it is, the equipment comes out of service until corrected. The rule also points to § 1926.1417. Safety devices and operational aids, item (xiv), follow a different path under §§ 1926.1415 and 1926.1416.
an immediate determination must be made by the competent person as to whether the deficiency constitutes a safety hazard.
If the deficiency is determined to constitute a safety hazard, the equipment must be taken out of service until it has been corrected.
